unresolved_claims.statement: The plugin adapter silently degrades on vendor B.
unresolved_claims.owner_question: When three vendors return three different verdicts on CLAIM-TRI-001, should the claim close as AMBIGUOUS-CLAIM rather than take a majority or casting vote
unresolved_claims.recommendation: Close CLAIM-TRI-001 as AMBIGUOUS-CLAIM. Do not treat any vendor as a casting vote.
unresolved_claims.strongest_tradeoff: A majority vote would manufacture a verdict the triangulation rule forbids; leaving the row open blocks every consumer that requires a terminal status.
unresolved_claims.default_if_unanswered: Close as AMBIGUOUS-CLAIM; do not count the claim as CONFIRMED or REFUTED.
unresolved_claims.impact: Downstream confirmation rates must keep CLAIM-TRI-001 out of both CONFIRMED and REFUTED denominators until an owner answer or a re-run of settle_claim.py changes the row.

settling_experiment.expected_observation: vendor_a_verdict, vendor_b_verdict and vendor_c_verdict are pairwise distinct.
settling_experiment.discriminating_outcome: Pairwise-distinct => keep AMBIGUOUS-CLAIM. Any two agreeing => the claim is no longer owner-escalation material.
settling_experiment.cost: one local process, under 30s, no vendor rail, no credential

unresolved_claims.statement: The hook contract fires twice on the same event under vendor C.
unresolved_claims.owner_question: Should CLAIM-TRI-002 stay owner-escalated while vendor C is NOT-CHECKED, instead of treating the two disagreeing vendors as a two-way vote
unresolved_claims.recommendation: Keep CLAIM-TRI-002 as IRREDUCIBLE until vendor C is checked or the owner accepts the two-way split as terminal.
unresolved_claims.strongest_tradeoff: Collapsing to a two-way vote silently drops the NOT-CHECKED prerequisite; waiting for vendor C delays every downstream gate that needs a terminal row.
unresolved_claims.default_if_unanswered: Keep IRREDUCIBLE; do not convert NOT-CHECKED into a casting vote.
unresolved_claims.impact: CNF-0161 consumers must not count CLAIM-TRI-002 as settled; the missing vendor-C check remains an explicit prerequisite.

settling_experiment.expected_observation: vendor_c_verdict is NOT-CHECKED while A and B disagree.
settling_experiment.discriminating_outcome: If vendor C becomes CONFIRMED or REFUTED and matches one side, the claim leaves the owner packet. If it remains NOT-CHECKED, the owner default stays IRREDUCIBLE.
settling_experiment.cost: one local process, under 30s, no vendor rail, no credential
